PATHWAY MODULATION: Strong evidence of pathway modulation through biomarker changes including ≥90% reduction in serum IgM levels, normalization of IgM, and disappearance of monoclonal protein - all consistent with effective B-cell receptor pathway inhibition in Waldenström's macroglobulinemia. 3. This suggests biological activity translated to clinical benefit, but not enough to reach statistical significance on the primary endpoint. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No clear subgroup differences identified, though the overall population appeared to respond to both BTK inhibitors. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This appears to be a head-to-head comparison trial that may have been underpowered to detect the observed difference in CR/VGPR rates.
